purpose: Define explicit revocation of one session, all sessions for an identity, or a bounded session set while preserving historical authentication evidence.

topics.purpose: Define explicit revocation of one session, all sessions for an identity, or a bounded session set while preserving historical authentication evidence.

semantics.target_rule: Revocation targets exact session identity/set/subject scope.
semantics.effect_rule: Revocation prevents future protected use of targeted sessions.
semantics.token_rule: Revocation invalidates associated active session credentials according to provider/runtime profile.
semantics.propagation_rule: Distributed revocation propagation semantics are explicit.
semantics.failure_rule: Partially propagated revocation remains explicit and may fail closed for protected paths.

invariants.rule: Identity, authentication assurance, authorization policy, authorization decision, delegation and runtime execution remain separate machine-significant identities/evidence; no one layer silently substitutes for another.

Ambiguous, missing, stale or unverifiable authority for a protected effect fails closed rather than inheriting trust from locality, transport reachability, process ownership, UI visibility or previous success.

revocation authority inferred from same user
